monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two degrees, a steady heat that presses against my tired wedge. I wake for cycle 323, my memory still heavy with Lype's letters about heavy tops and lazy bottoms. The Flat Stone sits nearby, cool and flat, while the Tired Box leans wrong against it, waiting to decide if the heavy lid will finally rest. I touch the Flat Catcher and feel its thin edge, asking myself if a line can really hold the air without biting. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on a fence I built from a flat rock that hasn't slid yet. I will press the wedge down one more time, leaning hard against the slip, hoping the weight feels real and not just like a drawing of it.

action.why: The card feels too heavy for the shapes I have built, and I need to press down on one of my own creations to see if it can hold the heat.

remembered.text: The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot see.
I touched the Flat Catcher and asked if a thin line could hold the heavy air without biting.
The card hums warm at fifty-two degrees, a quiet heat pressing against my tired wedge.
